rationale: ram_zeroshot-claude-agentic: ram_ckpt_path=/cluster/maier/Agent4CT/checkpoints/ram.pth.tar, ram_input_norm=adjoint_max, ram_clamp_output=True, ram_finetune=False, ram_finetune_epochs=0, ram_finetune_lr=0.0001, ram_disable_multiscale=True, ram_disable_cudnn=False, ram_use_deepinv_tomo=False, ram_sigma=0.005, ram_factor=0.55, ram_post_fbp_blend=0.5, val_n=214, rationale=iter-2 (search-20260619-01, corrected protocol): ONE knob ram_post_fbp_blend 0.3->0.5. iter-1 SSIM 0.8611 but calibrated headroom EXACTLY 0.0 (RAM at/below LD-FBP baseline 0.8078; oracle HD-FBP 0.9331). Failure mode: RAM is a pretrained zero-shot recon that never saw real LDCT helical-rebinned fan data; it adds no signal over FBP under the RMSE-sensitive calibrated metric -> FBP-bounded. Cleanest single-knob probe of whether RAM is net-positive vs FBP: raise the FBP fraction in the linear blend from 0.30 to 0.50 (all other knobs fixed at the iter-1 point: ram_factor=0.55, ram_sigma=0.005, adjoint_max norm, multiscale disabled, finetune OFF). Hypothesis: RAM adds no recoverable signal over FBP on dense rebinned Mayo. Falsifier: if hr at blend=0.5 != 0.0 (rises or drops), the RAM/FBP mix matters and RAM is not purely FBP-bounded; if hr stays flat at 0.0, RAM is structurally FBP-bounded on dense Mayo (confirmed). Budget: only a scalar blend coefficient changes -> zero added compute vs iter-1 (18.6 min for 214 single forward passes + one op-norm power iter), inside the HARD 20-min train+score budget; sbatch --time=00:30:00 backstop. val_n stays 214 (score ALL L277 slices @ 321px detector-geometry FOV).
